title: The Human Atmosphere; or, The Aura Made Visible by the Aid of Chemical Screens
author: Walter J. Kilner
edition_cited: New York: Rebman Company, 1911 (archive.org scan humanatmosphereo00kiln)
tradition: Edwardian medical aura research (St Thomas's Hospital); later adopted by aura-seeing schools
locator_hints: Chapter I 'The Aura of Healthy Persons', pp. 3-12 (c. 2-6% into file): the dicyanin ('spectauranine') screens; warning not to look through them continually; 'we gradually gained the power of seeing the Aura more and more plainly without the intervention of the screen'; room, lighting and background arrangements
Chapter on the Etheric Double and Inner/Outer Aura (c. 19-21%): use of carmine and blue screens by 'the observer who has gained the power of seeing the Aura without' the dicyanin screen
pp. 111-113 (c. 32-33%): loss of the power after a holiday and its quick return; visual-purple hypothesis; complementary-colour experiments
summary: A physician's manual for seeing a faint luminous envelope round the human body. The observer looks at daylight for some seconds through a glass cell of dicyanin dye, then views the unclothed subject against a black background in dim, diffuse light from one direction, standing with his back to a darkened window. Kilner reports that the dye's effect on the eyes is cumulative: he and his colleagues gradually came to see the aura more plainly without the screen and were finally able to dispense with it under suitable conditions; the power weakened after a holiday and returned quickly on resuming. He warns against looking through the screen continually because it harms the eyes, and offers a physiological theory (a change in visual purple extending sensitivity beyond the visible spectrum). He distinguishes an etheric double, an inner and an outer aura and describes their appearance and colours.
why_relevant: An eyes-open induction method (dye-screen pre-exposure plus dim-light viewing against black) with an explicit claim that the seen luminosity becomes independent of the aid; borderline on physical induction, so a test case for the inclusion rule.

date_evidence.basis: archive.org metadata date 1911 for the scanned first edition

notes: Kilner denies any occult faculty and treats the effect as optical. Dicyanin is no longer made and is toxic; the source itself reports eye damage. The reading agent should decide between keep_marginal and keep on the stimulus-independence claim.
